items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Those are the two best drummers that I ever sat on the outside of.

ctx.x: Who were some of the real steady drummers in that time, speaking of drummers? You know, they'd kept good time. Well I'm going to tell you about that. To my journey.

There's no drum player in this town right now, who plays much drum for me, is Dave Benny. Now I'm telling you my cousin Cy, and Alfred and all them, I'm telling you Dave Benny. Now I know how y'all feel about everybody else. Was he flashy or a straight drummer? He was everything. Everything? He was everything. David get half by their drums and he started to dance with them and he had to do that. They'd do that. Can they like it? Yeah, they'd explode, man. It was round. That's the only drummer I see all the men's…
How about Bunk? Really, did you ever play with Bunk? Did you ever see him after the time he got you to clarinet?
